items.title: Explainable Post-Disaster Grid Observability Recovery Using Human-Oversight Agentic LLMs
items.abstract: Post-disaster phasor measurement unit (PMU) outages reduce power-system observability and degrade operator situational awareness, requiring sequential restoration under limited resources. Existing PMU restoration methods based on optimization or heuristics can generate restoration schedules, but they often provide limited support for explanation, traceability, and operator interaction. This paper proposes an agentic tool-calling framework orchestrated by a large language model (LLM) for post-disaster PMU restoration and grid observability recovery. In this framework, the LLM does not directly solve the restoration optimization problem; instead, it coordinates validated backend tools required for post-disaster restoration, including observability assessment, restoration planning, state updates, and operator verification. The framework also maintains a structured tool-call history and execution context that keep restoration decisions traceable and explainable, while enabling context-aware operator question answering during the restoration process. Simulation results on IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 57-bus systems show that the proposed framework achieves observability recovery comparable to a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) solution, while providing tool-grounded explanations, interactive operator support, and human-overseen execution.

items.title: From Interface to Volition: Evaluating a HAPA-Based Persuasive Ecosystem for Children’s Oral Health Readiness
items.abstract: Effective pediatric oral health interventions require functional tools and psychological support to bridge the gap between intention and action. However, persuasive technologies often lack links between features and behavior change mechanisms. Grounded in the Health Action Process Approach (HAPA) and Persuasive Systems Design (PSD), this study evaluated a theory-driven eHealth ecosystem for oral care. We used a within-subject experiment with school-age children to compare the proposed system with a product and examine its immediate psychological determinants. Results showed the theory-driven system outperformed the control, activating action self-efficacy, intention, and planning constructs—“immediate cognitive readiness.” Under the age-stage grouping and testing arrangement, older children showed larger planning gains, especially coping planning gains, than younger children. By validating the “design-mechanism” alignment, this study links features with volitional processes. The findings offer a framework for auditing early stage eHealth effectiveness beyond engagement metrics to the verifiable psychological impact.

items.title: From Visit to Reflection: A Narrative Interaction Design Approach for Continuity in Virtual Museum Experiences with LLMs
items.abstract: Virtual museums have become an important form of cultural experience, yet narrative support often remains limited to individual exhibits or isolated phases of a visit. We define this as a problem of narrative continuity and address it through narrative interaction design. A multi-stakeholder formative study identified three design considerations: spatial structuring, relational interpretation, and reflective feedback. We instantiated these in NarraTour, a virtual museum prototype using bounded large language model-supported functions grounded in curated museum data and recorded interaction traces. A within-subject study (N = 24) across four configurations showed that spatial support establishes narrative progression, relational support is most effective when aligned with visitors’ progression, and reflective support extends continuity beyond exploration by enabling retrospective sense-making. We contribute a narrative interaction design approach for sustaining continuity across virtual museum experiences and empirical insights into when and how different forms of narrative support should be introduced.

items.title: Human Factors Evaluation Methods for Embodied Interaction Mediators: A Systematic Literature Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Human factors constructs such as workload, comfort, affect, trust, and agency are widely studied in HCI and HRI, yet their evaluation remains fragmented across embodied interaction mediator (EIM) communities. This systematic review synthesized 62 empirical studies of task-oriented robots, social robots, VR/AR mediators, and wearable mediators using a four-dimensional taxonomy of physical ergonomics, cognitive ergonomics, affect, and belief-related states. Two exploratory three-level meta-analyses were conducted. Meta-analysis I examined task-oriented-robot cognition studies (k = 8; g = 0.73, 95% CI [0.44, 1.02]), while Meta-analysis II examined target affective directions (k = 7; g = 0.67, 95% CI [−0.05, 1.40]). Neither showed a reliable objective–subjective difference. The findings are hypothesis-generating and reveal a Method-Construct Alignment Gap, supporting a construct-driven heuristic linking target constructs to primary and complementary evaluation methods.

items.title: Intrinsic Motivation in Reinforcement Learning: A Research Agenda for Adaptive Self-Organisation
items.abstract: Biological cells can be viewed as individual, interacting agents whose collective dynamics give rise to adaptive behaviour at multiple levels of organisation, from individual cells through tissues to whole multicellular organisms. In this perspective and tutorial article we discuss whether intrinsic rewards in artificial neural systems can support adaptation, functional specialisation and higher-level self-organisation without a shared external objective. We review empowerment, curiosity, learning progress, information gain, unsupervised skill discovery, mutual information estimation and the use of world models for intrinsic reward computation. Particular attention is given to failure modes showing when such objectives do not produce sustained exploration or increasingly complex behaviour. We argue that more capable systems may require complementary objectives, communication, memory, learning at multiple temporal scales and environmental constraints. Based on this perspective, we outline three experimental directions. These include a resource-constrained environment in which otherwise stable behavioural attractors become unsustainable, allowing us to test whether environmental constraints can mitigate characteristic failure modes of intrinsic objectives. The network of recurrent agents with per-agent intrinsic rewards, and a hierarchical world-model agent in which exploratory motor competence develops before goal-directed behaviour. These experiments are intended to test whether intrinsic learning can lead to adaptive organisation at progressively higher levels.

items.title: Level of Autonomy and Reliability in Co-located Multiple Robot Operation: A Five-Level Framework and Practical Design Guidance
items.abstract: Teleoperated robots augmented with autonomous assistance are increasingly used for conversational customer service in co-located deployments; we need a systematic method for determining which functions to automate and which to retain for the operator. We introduce a Level of Autonomy (LOA) framework with five levels and empirically examine how LOA and autonomy reliability jointly affect outcomes in co-located deployments. We conducted a laboratory study in which participants (N=32) acted as robot operators and, via a teleoperated robot in a simulated shop, engaged in conversational product recommendation interactions using a teleoperation interface. We compared five LOA conditions across multiple reliability conditions and measured the NASA-TLX, System Usability Scale (SUS), interpersonal effects, and task performance. The results show that when reliability is high, the most effective strategy was either to fully automate the target function or to keep operator control minimal and clearly bounded; designs that required operators to both supervise the automation and intervene frequently tended to increase workload. In addition, in early deployments, when operators are unfamiliar with teleoperation, avoid designs that require frequent operator decisions. When reliability is limited, lower LOA was preferable, reducing mode-switching between error recovery and normal teleoperation. This study provides a five-level LOA framework for co-located multi-robot customer service and suggests that effective customer-facing HRI in such settings requires aligning LOA with autonomy reliability and clear human-robot role allocation.

items.title: MindCare+: A Digital Phenotyping Framework for Mental Health Monitoring and Support in Indonesia
items.abstract: Background: Indonesia has a substantial adolescent mental health burden and a large service gap. The Indonesia-National Adolescent Mental Health Survey estimated that 34.9% of adolescents had a mental health problem and 5.5% met criteria for a mental disorder in the previous 12 months [1,2]. Only 2.6% of adolescents with a mental health problem had accessed support or counselling services [1]. Smartphone and wearable sensing can capture longitudinal behavioral and physiological signals, but current digital phenotyping evidence is heterogeneous and remains constrained by missingness, limited external validation, and uncertain clinical utility [3–7]. Objective: To reformulate the original MindCare+ student innovation concept into an evidence-bounded, human-supervised research architecture for longitudinal mental health risk monitoring and stepped psychological support in Indonesia. Methods: We used an evidence-informed conceptual framework-development approach. The original proposal was decomposed into sensing, interpretation, screening, support, professional integration, governance, and implementation domains. Targeted literature was used to classify proposed functions as near-term capabilities, translational hypotheses, or functions that should not be assumed without prospective validation. No participant-level data were generated and no efficacy analysis was performed. Results: MindCare+ is specified as a consent-based closed loop linking smartphone-derived behavioral features, optional wearable physiology, active validated self-report, data-quality and privacy gating, longitudinal personal baselines, contextual multimodal interpretation, visible uncertainty, stepped support, and human escalation. Passive signals are treated as risk-relevant context rather than psychiatric labels. Active screening is used as an additional assessment layer rather than a diagnosis. A staged validation pathway is proposed from data capture reliability and psychometric localization through prospective clinical comparison, human-factors testing, fairness and privacy evaluation, and controlled implementation. Conclusions: MindCare+ should be evaluated as a research program rather than as an autonomous mental health detector. Its central testable question is whether privacy-preserving longitudinal sensing, combined with active screening and meaningful human oversight, can improve recognition of clinically relevant change and access to appropriate support without producing unacceptable false alerts, surveillance burden, inequity, or harm.

items.title: Musculoskeletal Discomfort and Usability of an Intraoperative Neck and Back Support Exoskeleton: A Multisite Study
items.abstract: Surgeons are at high risk of developing long-term Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs) due to awkward sustained postures. Passive spine-supporting exoskeletons are a potential intervention to improve posture and reduce fatigue. The NekSpine ® was evaluated by 21 surgeons (15 male) across two hospital sites within a quaternary academic hospital system. Each surgeon performed at least two comparable procedures, one with the exoskeleton and one without. Surgeons completed pre- and postoperative surveys assessing NASA-TLX workload, usability, body-part discomfort, overall fatigue, and workflow disruptions. Eighty-two cases were evaluated (43 exoskeleton cases). Compared with baseline cases, surgeons reported reduced neck and upper back discomfort and lower overall fatigue when using the exoskeleton. The NekSpine ® exoskeleton may reduce spinal discomfort and fatigue during surgery, supporting its potential as an ergonomic intervention for surgeons.

items.title: Old argumentative plays on a new field? Contributions from sport ethics to the ethical analysis of artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract In the ethics of artificial intelligence, a recurring anxiety concerns the deskilling argument: the worry that delegating distinctively human tasks to AI erodes valuable capacities and there by diminishes meaning. This article argues that philosophy of sport offers underutilized but illuminating resources for analyzing this concern. Drawing ondebates over biomedical enhancement in sport ethics, I identify four argumentative strategies—centered on the values of agency, effort, natural talent, and narrativity—that sport philosophers have developed to evaluate themoral costs of skill-displacing technology. These “old plays,” I contend, can be productively transplanted onto the “new field” of AI ethics, where analogous debates about skill erosion, meritocracy, difficulty, and human identityremain contested. items.title: The impact of partial automation and cognitive load on drivers’ visual search strategies in an urban driving environment
items.abstract: Non-visual cognitive tasks (e.g., hands-free phone conversations) are well known to impair drivers' visual search in manual driving, but evidence in partially automated driving (PAD) remains inconsistent and limited, especially in complex driving environments that demand active visual scanning. In a driving-simulator study, we examined how automation and cognitive load (2-back task) shape visual-search strategies in a busy urban setting with frequent distractors and potential hazards, using both temporal and sequential scanning measures. Unlike findings from monotonous driving contexts, PAD drivers broadened their visual search without trading off attention to the forward road. Under cognitive load, their attention to peripheral roadway declined more sharply than in manual driving, leading to restricted visual search across both driving modes. Our results underscore the influence of non-visual distraction on drivers' visual scanning during PAD in complex environments and highlight the value of eye-tracking-based features for monitoring cognitive load.

items.title: Tracking the Unseen: An Occlusion-Robust Framework for Target Tracking Under Full and Long-Term Occlusion
items.abstract: Real-time multi-object tracking systems remain highly vulnerable to full and long-term occlusion, where targets temporarily or completely disappear from the camera's field of view. Conventional trackers may terminate trajectories prematurely, resulting in identity loss and reduced situational awareness in applications such as defense and surveillance. This work proposes an occlusion-robust target tracking framework that maintains target identity and trajectory continuity through the integration of YOLOv11n object detection, Kalman Filter motion prediction, and occlusion-aware appearance-based re-identification. The framework consists of three stages: object detection, position estimation during occlusion, and identity recovery after target reappearance. Six Re-Identification (Re-ID) architectures were evaluated within the same tracking framework under identical conditions, with the Occlusion-Aware Mask Network (OAMN) achieving the best overall performance and therefore selected for the final pipeline. The framework was benchmarked against OccluTrack on the public OVIS dataset, achieving relative improvements of 18.1 percent in Multiple Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) and 25.1 percent in Identity F1 Score (IDF1), while reducing identity switches by 12.8 percent. On a custom military dataset simulating surveillance and battlefield-like environments with long-term occlusion, the framework achieved a MOTA of 0.734 and an IDF1 of 0.729, corresponding to relative improvements of 14.2 percent and 5.8 percent over OccluTrack. The system demonstrated strong tracking continuity, robust identity preservation, and reliable trajectory estimation under challenging occlusion conditions, highlighting its effectiveness for defense-related surveillance applications requiring continuous target tracking during visibility loss.

items.title: Unspoken Into the Spoken: Visualizing Cultural Nuances in Intercultural Romantic Dyads Through Generative AI-Driven Art
items.abstract: Intercultural romantic partners often face subtle emotional misunderstandings shaped by cultural norms that are difficult to articulate. Building on research on generative AI for reflective meaning-making, we investigate how a multimodal AI probe combining journaling, metaphorical visualization, and partner dialogue can help dyads externalize and reflect on culturally rooted experiences. Drawing on 28 academic papers and over 40 social media narratives, we identified eight recurring themes of cultural tension and designed a probe around prompts. In a six-day diary study with 14 participants (7 dyads), participants moved across textual journaling, AI-generated visual abstraction, and dialogue to support perspective-taking and situated co-interpretation of self, partner, and relationship. With repeated use, some dyads shifted from treating images as standalone artifacts to using them as prompts for sharing hidden narratives. We derive design implications for sustained intercultural reflection while emphasizing generated artifacts as provisional prompts rather than authoritative interpretations of emotions or culture.

items.title: Will They or Won’t They? Exploring Pedestrian Dilemma Zones in a Virtual Reality Crossing Experiment
items.abstract: Pedestrian fatalities in the United States rose 80% between 2009 and 2023, far outpacing the 13% increase in all other traffic deaths. A pedestrian’s ability to distinguish crossable from non-crossable gaps varies with the time between the pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle. Intermediate gaps can create uncertainty, leading to riskier decisions. This range is called the dilemma zone. While the dilemma zone has been studied in naturalistic environments, no work has systematically examined it in a controlled virtual environment. The proposed study uses virtual reality to manipulate vehicle speed and size and to explore how judgment certainty shifts within the dilemma zone. Sixty participants will complete a three-phase, within-subjects experiment estimating walking speed, critical gap, and crossing decisions across gap sizes. We hypothesize that larger and faster vehicles will increase both the critical gap and the width of the dilemma zone. Findings may inform roadway design and traffic-calming strategies.

items.title: Perceived AI Legitimacy and Trust in Human–AI Decision Assistance: A Dual-Path Perspective on Psychological and Normative Evaluation
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) increasingly supports decision-making, users evaluate not only the system’s performance and trustworthiness but also the legitimacy and appropriateness of AI decision processes. This study examines how Perceived AI Legitimacy (PAL) is associated with reliance-oriented decision-assistance intention through cognitive and affective trust, while examining the moderating role of personal need for structure (PNS). Survey data from 1,000 Korean adults with GenAI experience were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. PAL was positively associated with both trust dimensions and indirectly with intention through both, with a numerically larger indirect association through cognitive trust. PAL retained a small direct association, while PNS negatively moderated the affective trust–intention association. These findings indicate that willingness to incorporate AI-generated judgments reflects differentiated roles of legitimacy, competence-based confidence, and affective reassurance, with individual differences shaping how these factors relate to intention, although these associations should be interpreted as correlational.

items.title: When a voice agent becomes a flight instructor: Effects of instructor and expertise in simulated flight training
items.abstract: Voice agents (VAs) are increasingly used in learning, training, and human-AI interaction. In this study, a VA instructor for simulated flight training was designed to examine training performance and experience compared with a human instructor. The effects of learners' expertise in flight knowledge and simulated flight experience were also investigated. Sixty-eight participants took part in a between-subjects experiment to learn simulated flight in an aircraft simulator with different instructor types. Subjective ratings, objective flight data, and physiological data were collected. The results showed that participants reported positive attitudes toward learning with the VA. Learner expertise influenced mental model development and subjective task load, with participants of higher expertise demonstrating more complete mental models and lower task load. Instructor type was also associated with learning experience and flight behavior. Compared with the human instructor, VA instruction showed directional patterns toward lower subjective task load and higher flight velocity, with comparable overall training outcomes. These findings support the feasibility of VA-based instruction in simulated flight training and highlight its potential as an instructional agent in complex human-computer interaction environments.

items.title: A Decade in Review: Situation-Awareness-Based Agent Transparency and Human-Machine Teaming
items.abstract: Over the past decade, the Situation awareness-based Agent Transparency (SAT) framework has become a foundational model for the design of effective human-machine systems. As machine autonomy increases, the opaque nature of artificial intelligence can impede collaboration. The SAT framework addresses this challenge through a three-level structure—Perception, Comprehension, and Projection—that clarifies an agent’s reasoning and intent for human partners. This article reviews a decade of research applying the SAT model across domains such as human-robot interaction and autonomous driving. Findings consistently indicate that SAT-based transparency enhances team performance, improves operator situation awareness, and fosters calibrated trust, often without increasing cognitive workload. The model has evolved from a unidirectional tool to a dynamic, bidirectional paradigm that enables genuine human-agent teaming. Future research should focus on developing adaptive transparency, refining human-to-agent communication, and investigating long-term effects to create more effective and responsible systems.

items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education has increased the need to strengthen teacher training to ensure its effective pedagogical implementation. This study aimed to analyze recent scientific evidence on teacher training in AI and its contribution to educational quality. A qualitative systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, including twenty Scopus-indexed studies published between 2023 and 2025. The findings indicate that AI literacy, continuous professional development, and active training strategies constitute the main pillars of teacher preparation. The evidence also shows that AI enhances personalized learning, inclusion, and pedagogical innovation when implemented within sound ethical principles and pedagogical foundations. It is concluded that teacher training represents a key factor in achieving the responsible and sustainable integration of artificial intelligence aimed at strengthening educational quality.

items.abstract: Resumen: El examen de textos contemporáneos africanos traducidos aborda la cuestión de términos relacionados unos a otros al tiempo que determinan la noción de identidad en traducción. Transferir un contenido literario del francés al español puede ocasionar varios resultados conducentes cada uno a una determinada identidad del traductor. Cada elección tiene la particularidad de presentar una imagen diferente del autor del texto traducido. A veces libre de sus decisiones y en otras ocasiones despojado de esta libertad, el traductor puede navegar entre una visibilidad cultural del texto fuente o permanecer completamente oculto en el texto meta. Pero en cualquiera de sus manifestaciones, presenta una determinada identidad que depende de la ideología y de los factores implicados en las decisiones adoptadas en cada momento. Palabras clave: Identidad del traductor; traducción literaria; domesticación; extranjerización; ideología del traductor.

items.title: Consolidation Without Weights: What the Complementary Learning Systems Analogy Licenses in LLM Agent Memory, and Why the Systems That Borrow Its Name Do Not Inherit Its Guarantee
items.abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Memory systems for language-model agents almost all contain a step called consolidation, and almost all of them cite, or gesture at, the complementary learning systems account of hippocampus and neocortex when they name it. In that account consolidation is a specific operation: repeated replay from a fast, sparsely coded store into a slow learner whose shared parameters change, which is what produces generalisation to material never stored and which is also where interference lives. This paper separates what that theory commits its borrower to from what agent memory systems actually do. Four commitments are stated and used as an audit instrument. Against them, deployed agent memory divides into two families and neither instantiates the mechanism, for opposite reasons. The larger, textual family changes no parameters at all: its consolidation is iterated LLM-authored rewriting of an external store, and a 2026 controlled study reports that iterating it drives utility up and then down, in their setting below the no-memory baseline, while no replay result located here reports falling below its own no-replay control. A smaller parametric family, which appeared during 2026 and falsifies the common claim that agent memory never touches weights, does change parameters, but most of it buys stability through per-task adapter isolation or expandable blocks, and isolation withholds the shared representation that the source theory identifies as the common cause of interference and generalisation alike. The paper argues that the field's avoidance of online parametric transfer is well supported by evidence about what such transfer costs, and that what is not supported is retaining the vocabulary while declining the mechanism. It states the five measurements that would decide the question and identifies the single published configuration whose shape matches the theory. items.title: Culturally and linguistically adaptive AI and professional capital among language educators
items.abstract: Purpose This study explores how culturally and linguistically adaptive artificial intelligence (AI) systems align with patterns of professional capital—human, social, and decisional—among language educators in under-resourced, multilingual contexts. It examines how educators' engagement with the AI platform relates to knowledge development, collaborative networks, and instructional decision-making while considering infrastructural constraints and equity challenges. Design/methodology/approach A qualitatively driven multiple-case study involving 48 language educators (16 per region) from Iran, India, and rural Kenya/Tanzania was conducted. Data from semi-structured interviews, focus groups, and AI platform logs documenting feedback, collaboration and analytics were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis in NVivo. AI platform log data contextualized qualitative interpretations rather than testing statistical relationships. Triangulation, member checking and reflexive journaling supported the credibility and trustworthiness of the findings. Findings Educators' engagement with the AI platform aligned with patterns of professional capital across three dimensions: human capital through context-aware pedagogical feedback (85% engaged with feedback features), social capital through peer collaboration (75% engaged with peer-feedback features) and decisional capital through access to analytic summaries (92% accessed analytics features). Qualitative findings further suggested that professional capital emerged through the interaction of adaptive AI, sociocultural context, and infrastructural conditions. Originality/value This study contributes empirical insights into the application of professional capital theory within AI-supported professional learning in multilingual and under-resourced educational settings. By highlighting the interaction between adaptive AI design and sociocultural contexts, the study advances understanding of culturally responsive AI integration and offers practical implications for developing more equitable, resilient, and context-responsive learning environments.

items.title: Negotiating GenAI in rural secondary schools in Indonesia: EFL teachers’ positioning, identity, and agency
items.abstract: The rapid emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping educational practices, including language education. While existing research has largely examined GenAI’s instructional affordances and ethical implications, less attention has been paid to how teachers experience, interpret, and respond to these changes, particularly in under-resourced contexts. This study examined how EFL teachers in rural Indonesian secondary schools enact agency, construct professional identity, and position themselves in relation to the emergence of GenAI. A qualitative case study was employed to examine three rural EFL teachers using a series of semi-structured interviews conducted over a nine-month period. The data were then analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Informed by positioning theory and teacher identity and agency, the analysis explores how teachers discursively construct their professional roles, position students, and assign pedagogical meaning to GenAI. Three interrelated themes were identified. First, teachers negotiate GenAI’s pedagogical value, recognising its efficiency for instructional support while expressing concern about superficial learning and cognitive development. Second, they preserve professional identity by positioning themselves as guardians of students’ cognitive integrity, enacting protective agency against premature reliance on GenAI. Third, they adapt to rural realities of integration, where infrastructural constraints, school policies, and students’ informal digital practices shape the conditions of use. The study advances theoretical understandings of teacher agency by highlighting how identity and positioning processes mediate teachers’ responses to GenAI and offers insights for supporting AI integration in under-resourced educational contexts.

items.title: Non-profit work of the future? Scientific considerations of AI deployment in sectors with limited resources
items.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can be meaningfully implemented in non-profit and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) operating under resource constraints. This study explores how AI may contribute to efficiency gains and workload reduction while preserving the mission-driven and relational character of social work. This study also addresses barriers such as financial limitations, lack of technical expertise and ethical concerns, situating NGO digital transformation within broader debates on the common good and sociotechnical change. Design/methodology/approach The mixed-methods project KINiro (AI for NGOs), funded by the German Federal Ministry for Family Affairs, used a sequential qual → QUAN → qual design. Data were gathered through a scoping review, exploratory interviews (n = 5), an online survey (n = 335) and in-depth expert interviews (n = 10). Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively; qualitative data were coded using Kuckartz’s content analysis. The results provide a comprehensive picture of current AI adoption, expectations and challenges within German NGOs. Findings Most NGOs are in the early stages of AI adoption. Around 60% have experimented with AI, mainly for writing support, translation and research. Of organizations, 45.1% reported occasional AI use, 14.8% regular use and 7.6% planned future use. Perceived benefits include automation of routine tasks and resource conservation. Concerns center on data protection, loss of control and “dehumanization” of social interaction. Overall, AI evokes ambivalence – simultaneously hope for relief and fear of ethical risks. Research limitations/implications The findings of this study are based on German NGOs and may not fully generalize internationally. Further comparative research is needed to assess cross-cultural differences in AI acceptance and governance. Practical implications Results highlight the need for targeted funding, digital roadmaps and participatory implementation processes involving employees and volunteers to ensure sustainable AI integration. Social implications Ethically aligned AI use can strengthen civil-society organizations by enhancing efficiency without undermining human-centered values, thus supporting democratic and social participation. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides one of the first empirical analyses of AI in NGOs, integrating ethical, organizational and resource perspectives. This study contributes to computer ethics by framing NGO digitalization as a sociotechnical and common-good issue rather than a purely technological challenge.
